what: Lactation curve — milk yield over DIM
title: Introduction to VirtualDairyHerdR
text: Using longitudinal = TRUE generate full time series (one row per cow per DIM), plotting Wood’s curve sample cows.
code: herd_long <- simulate_herd(n_cows = 30, longitudinal = TRUE, seed = 42) milk_long <- simulate_milk(herd_long, seed = 42)  # Sample 6 cows for clarity sample_cows <- unique(milk_long$cow_id)[1:6]  milk_long |>   dplyr::filter(cow_id %in% sample_cows) |>   ggplot(aes(x = days_in_milk, y = milk_kg, colour = cow_id)) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +   labs(     title  = "Lactation curves — daily milk yield over DIM",     x      = "Days in Milk",     y      = "Milk yield (kg)",     colour = "Cow ID"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Simulate Fertility Records — simulate_fertility

title: Simulate Lactation Curves — simulate_lactation

title: Simulate Lactation Curves — simulate_lactation
text: herd tibble produced simulate_herd(). seed Integer. Random seed reproducibility. Default NULL.

title: Simulate Lactation Curves — simulate_lactation
text: input tibble additional columns: wood_a, wood_b, wood_c, peak_dim, peak_yield, predicted_yield.

title: Simulate Lactation Curves — simulate_lactation
text: Wood's model: Y = * DIM^b * exp(-c * DIM) wood_a — scale parameter (drives overall yield level) wood_b — inclining slope (time peak) wood_c — declining slope (persistency) peak_dim — predicted day peak yield = b / c peak_yield — predicted peak yield kg Breed lactation adjustments applied wood_a. Individual cow-level random effects added three parameters.

title: Simulate Lactation Curves — simulate_lactation
code: herd <- simulate_herd(100, seed = 1) lact <- simulate_lactation(herd, seed = 1)
